Industrial Dispute

Some 23 workers employed by the Sin Kang Printing Works, 477-481 Sinza Road, submitted to their management the following demands:-

(1) That an increase be given of $30 each in wages to those who earned $20 to $39 per month and of $26 each to those earned more than $40 per month.

(2) That three tenths of a picul of rice at the basic price of $40 be granted to each worker.

(3) That no workers be dismissed without just cause.

(4) That working hours be reduced to eight instead of nine hours, to five instead of six hours in night-work and full day's rest on Sundays with full pay.

(5) That wages be paid during sick leave.

(6) That allowances for apprentices be increased to $9 per month for the first year, $12 per month for the second year, and $15 per month for the third year.

Two workers' representatives, named Tong Sheng (湯勝) and Ching Ih Chang (金益璋), called in the office of the Industrial & Social Division on July 26th, 1941 and submitted a petition requesting mediation.

Negotiations between the management, represented by Mr. Peh Shwen Yung (白純熊), and two workers' representatives took place in the Division Office at 3:00 p.m. July 28th, and 11:00 a.m. July 29th. Mr. Peh stated that he has granted an increase in wages to all workers in April, 1941 and a further increase in allowances in May. The management also provides food and sleeping accommodation. He refused to consider their demands. Thus a deadlock was then reached.

Some 12 out of 23 workers declared a strike at 1:00 p.m. July 30th, in order to enforce the above demands for better treatment.

（印：SPECIAL BRANCH 1941）

劳资纠纷

受雇于新闸路477-481号新康印刷所的约23名工人向管理层提交了以下要求：-

(1) 月薪在20至39美元之间的工人，每人加薪30美元；月薪超过40美元的工人，每人加薪26美元。

(2) 按基本价格40美元计算，向每名工人发放0.3担大米。

(3) 无正当理由不得解雇任何工人。

(4) 工作时间由九小时减为八小时，夜班由六小时减为五小时，星期日全天休息且照发工资。

(5) 病假期间照发工资。

(6) 学徒津贴增加至第一年每月9美元，第二年每月12美元，第三年每月15美元。

两名工人代表，名为汤胜（Tong Sheng）和金益璋（Ching Ih Chang），于1941年7月26日前往工业与社会处办公室，提交请愿书请求调解。

由白纯熊（Peh Shwen Yung）先生代表的管理层与两名工人代表之间的谈判，于7月28日下午3时及7月29日上午11时在该处办公室进行。白先生表示，他已于1941年4月给所有工人加了薪，并于5月进一步增加了津贴。管理层还提供食宿。他拒绝考虑他们的要求。因此陷入僵局。

为了强制执行上述改善待遇的要求，23名工人中的约12名于7月30日下午1时宣布罢工。

Further to:
    Labour Unrest amongst Employees of the
    Sing Kong Press, No.477-481 Sinza Road.

    On the A.M. of 30-7-41., a letter was received
from the Management of the Sing Kong Press, which stated
that the strike had now been settled on the following
conditions:-

1. No employee will be dismissed without justification.
2. Commencing from August 1, 1942, the management will
   consider an increase for all employees according to
   their living conditions.
3. The employees will not go on strike or create any
   disturbance.
4. Employees will not be absent from work for more than
   four days per month, except through sickness, which
   is to be certified by an authorised doctor.

    Letter and translation attached.
    Copy to Special Branch (direct).

Translation of Attached Letter

July 30, 1941.

Sinza Police Station,
Sirs,
    We beg to inform you that the strike which took
place amongst our employees has now been settled at 11:20
a.m. this inst. (July 30, 1941), through the mediation of
Messrs Ching Teang Foo and Chang Kya Yih, with the result
that all workers have resumed work.
    The efforts made by you to protect our shop are much
appreciated by us, and we hereby convey to you our hearty
thanks.

From Sing Kong Press.

Labour Unrest amongst employees of the
Sing Kong Press, No.477-481 Sinsa Road.

At 1 p.m. on the 28-7-41., C.P.C. 2436 brought to
the station a male Chinese named Mo Bao Kung (馬宝根),
36, Shanghai, M/print-setter, employed and residing at
the Sing Kong (新康) Press, No.477-481 Sinsa Road,
whom he arrested at 12:45 p.m. for posting notices
bearing the following inscriptions, on the wall outside
the latter premises:-

1. We request the capitalists to realize our poor
conditions and to grant us a satisfactory reply.
2. Protect our representatives.
3. We demand better treatment.
4. Capitalists and labourers should co-operate
together.
5. We demand to be released from our hardships.

On the culprit being questioned he admitted posting
the notices on the wall on the instructions of other two
employees, named (1) Ching Yih Tsang (金益樟), print-
setter, and (2) Taung Sung (湯勝), printer, also
employed and residing on the premises.

Further enquiries revealed that the Sing Kong Press
is owned and managed by Pah Sung Yoong (白維熊). He
employs 17 workers, who are all members of the Printing
Products Labour Union (印刷業產業工會), office situated
in Gwepei. Six apprentices are also employed, but they

新闸路477-481号新康印刷所（Sing Kong Press）雇员中的劳工骚动。

1941年7月28日下午1时，中央巡逻车警员2436号将一名名叫马宝根（Mo Bao Kung）的中国男子带至捕房，该男子36岁，上海人，职业为排字工，受雇并居住于新闸路477-481号新康（Sin Kang）印刷所。他于中午12时45分被捕，原因是他在该场所外的墙上张贴了写有以下内容的告示：-

1. 我们请求资本家体察我们的困苦处境，并给予我们满意的答复。
2. 保护我们的代表。
3. 我们要求改善待遇。
4. 资本家与劳动者应通力合作。
5. 我们要求从苦难中解脱。

经讯问，该罪犯承认是受另外两名雇员的指示在墙上张贴告示，这两名雇员分别是：(1) 金益樟（Ching Yih Tsang），排字工，和 (2) 汤胜（Taung Sung），印刷工，他们也受雇并居住在该场所内。

进一步调查显示，新康印刷所为白维熊（Pah Sung Yoong）所有并管理。他雇佣了17名工人，这些工人均为印刷业产业工会（Printing Products Labour Union）会员，该工会办事处位于闸北（Gwepei）。还雇佣了六名学徒，但他们
